teaching_point: Melasma: symmetrical light-to-dark brown macular patches on sun-exposed face — centrofacial pattern (forehead, cheeks, upper lip, nose, chin) is the commonest.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Malar melasma on the cheeks — triggers: UV and visible light, hormones (pregnancy, COC/HRT), genetics; daily broad-spectrum SPF (tinted for visible light) is foundational.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Melasma on the forehead with irregular geographic edges — Wood's lamp enhancement suggests epidermal pigment; mixed/dermal types respond less well.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Melasma — chronic relapsing course; set expectations: control not cure; heat, visible light and stopping treatment provoke relapse.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Melasma (chloasma) in pregnancy/hormonal context — often fades post-partum; avoid hydroquinone and retinoids in pregnancy, use sun protection and camouflage.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Extensive melasma — specialist options (Kligman-type triple combination short courses, oral tranexamic acid off-label, peels/lasers with caution) belong in dermatology.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Melasma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/melasma

teaching_point: Exogenous ochronosis after long-term hydroquinone: blue-black/grey-brown speckled pigmentation on the very areas being "lightened" — paradoxical darkening; stop hydroquinone and refer.
dermnet_caption: Ochronosis following long-term use of hydroquinone
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Ochronosis following long-term use of hydroquinone (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alkaptonuria-and-ochronosis

teaching_point: Exogenous ochronosis — often from unlicensed high-strength/long-duration bleaching creams; very hard to reverse; biopsy shows yellow-brown banana-shaped dermal fibres.
dermnet_caption: Ochronosis following long-term use of hydroquinone
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Ochronosis following long-term use of hydroquinone (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alkaptonuria-and-ochronosis

teaching_point: Dermoscopy of hydroquinone ochronosis: blue-grey amorphous areas and dots/globules obliterating follicular openings — a clue vs melasma.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy of ochronosis (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/alkaptonuria-and-ochronosis

teaching_point: Nail pigmentation due to hydroquinone — another clue to (often undeclared) bleaching-product use; ask directly and non-judgementally.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nail pigmentation due to hydroquinone (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hydroquinone

teaching_point: Phototoxic drug eruption (oral NSAID): exaggerated sunburn on exposed sites that can heal with pigmentation — review drug list (tetracyclines, thiazides, amiodarone, NSAIDs, sulfonylureas).
dermnet_caption: A phototoxic drug eruption due to an oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A phototoxic drug eruption due to an oral non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/drug-induced-photosensitivity

teaching_point: Photosensitive drug eruption sparing skin under a watch and strap — sharp cut-off at clothing/accessories points to light as the trigger.
dermnet_caption: A photosensitive drug eruption showing sparing under the watch and strap
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A photosensitive drug eruption showing sparing under the watch and strap (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/drug-induced-photosensitivity

teaching_point: Photoallergic contact dermatitis to fragrance in aftershave — fragrance is a classic sensitiser behind Riehl-type pigmented cosmetic dermatitis in darker skin (proxy image: DermNet has no dedicated Riehl melanosis photo).
dermnet_caption: Photoallergic contact dermatitis due to a fragrance in an aftershave
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Photoallergic contact dermatitis due to a fragrance in an aftershave (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/photocontact-dermatitis

teaching_point: Fragrance contact allergy on the neck (perfume-application site) — in skin of colour chronic low-grade allergy can present mainly as grey-brown pigmentation rather than red eczema.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Contact allergy on neck (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/fragrance-allergy

teaching_point: Patch testing: allergen chambers applied to the upper back, removed at 48 h, read at 48 h and ~96 h — the key investigation for suspected pigmented contact dermatitis (refer to a contact dermatitis clinic).
dermnet_caption: Patch test strips in place after application
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Patch test strips in place after application (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/patch-tests

teaching_point: Strong (+++) positive patch test to fragrance mix — guides precise avoidance advice (INCI label reading, fragrance-free products).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Fragrance mix II +++ (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/fragrance-allergy

teaching_point: Black skin staining from the hair-dye allergen PPD at a patch-test site — PPD and kumkum are frequently implicated in pigmented contact dermatitis; photopatch testing adds UVA irradiation when photoallergy is suspected.
dermnet_caption: Black skin staining due to the hair dye allergen PPD
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Black skin staining due to the hair dye allergen PPD (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/patch-tests

teaching_point: Lichen planus pigmentosus on the face: ill-defined slate-grey to grey-brown macules, little preceding inflammation — South Asian/Middle Eastern adults; biopsy shows lichenoid interface change + pigment incontinence.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planus pigmentosus of face (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planus

teaching_point: Lichen planus pigmentosus on the lower back — part of acquired dermal macular hyperpigmentation (ADMH); flexural "inversus" variant also occurs.
dermnet_caption: Lichen planus pigmentosus of lower back
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planus pigmentosus of lower back (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acquired-dermal-macular-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: Lichen planus pigmentosus of the lower lip — rare mucosal pattern; check oral mucosa for classic lichen planus.
dermnet_caption: Lichen planus pigmentosus of lower lip
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planus pigmentosus of lower lip (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lichen-planus

teaching_point: Acquired dermal macular hyperpigmentation — umbrella for LPP, erythema dyschromicum perstans and idiopathic eruptive macular pigmentation; dermal pigment responds poorly to topical lighteners.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acquired dermal macular hyperpigmentation (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/acquired-dermal-macular-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: Erythema dyschromicum perstans (ashy dermatosis): symmetrical ash-grey oval macules on trunk/proximal limbs, sometimes with an early red rim — asymptomatic, chronic.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema dyschromicum perstans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-dyschromicum-perstans

teaching_point: Ashy dermatosis on the trunk — favours sun-protected sites (vs LPP on face/flexures); reassure, sun protect, specialist options limited.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema dyschromicum perstans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-dyschromicum-perstans

teaching_point: Erythema dyschromicum perstans close-up — grey-blue dermal pigment; differentials: LPP, fixed drug eruption, PIH, Hansen disease in endemic contexts.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Erythema dyschromicum perstans (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/erythema-dyschromicum-perstans

teaching_point: Phytophotodermatitis: bizarre streaky erythema where plant sap/juice (furocoumarins) met sunlight — odd linear/drip shapes are the diagnostic clue.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Streaky erythema on the arm (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/phytophotodermatitis

teaching_point: Linear redness and blisters after strimming (giant hogweed/parsnip/rue sap) — UK summer presentation; cool compresses, potent topical steroid short course, sun avoidance.
dermnet_caption: Linear redness and blisters from strimming
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Linear redness and blisters from strimming (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/phytophotodermatitis

teaching_point: Acute bullous phytophotodermatitis on the ankle — large blisters need dressing and review; consider burn-type management if extensive.
dermnet_caption: Acute bullous phytophotodermatitis on the ankle
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Acute bullous phytophotodermatitis on the ankle (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/phytophotodermatitis

teaching_point: Phototoxic dermatitis from lime juice on a sunny day ("margarita dermatitis") — drip/hand-print shapes; may be mistaken for burns or non-accidental injury in children.
dermnet_caption: Phototoxic contact dermatitis due to accidental lime juice contact on a sunny day
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Phototoxic contact dermatitis due to accidental lime juice contact on a sunny day (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/photocontact-dermatitis

teaching_point: Post-inflammatory pigmentation after phytophotodermatitis — can persist for months; sun protection and reassurance; often the stage at which patients present.
dermnet_caption: Postinflammatory pigmentation after resolution of phytophotodermatitis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Postinflammatory pigmentation after resolution of phytophotodermatitis (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/phytophotodermatitis

teaching_point: Lime-juice phytophotodermatitis leaving pigmented streaks on the chest — ask about holidays, cocktails, gardening, celery/parsnip handling.
dermnet_caption: Postinflammatory pigmentation from lime juice phytophotoderatitis on the chest
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Postinflammatory pigmentation from lime juice phytophotoderatitis on the chest (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/phytophotodermatitis

teaching_point: Macular amyloidosis: rippled grey-brown pigmentation on the upper chest/back — linked to chronic friction (nylon scrubbers, towels) in skin of colour; stop friction, treat itch.
dermnet_caption: Rippled pigmentation on the upper chest due to macular amyloidosis
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Rippled pigmentation on the upper chest due to macular amyloidosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-amyloidosis

teaching_point: Macular amyloidosis over the interscapular back — classic "rippled" reticulate pattern; biopsy with Congo red (apple-green birefringence) confirms keratin-derived amyloid.
dermnet_caption: Macular amyloidosis showing rippled pigmentation over the upper back
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Macular amyloidosis showing rippled pigmentation over the upper back (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-amyloidosis

teaching_point: Macular amyloidosis secondary to repeated scratching of notalgia paraesthetica — itch–scratch cycle drives it; manage the itch.
dermnet_caption: Repetitive scratching of an area of notalgia paraesthetica resulting in macular amyloidosis on the back
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Repetitive scratching of an area of notalgia paraesthetica resulting in macular amyloidosis on the back (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-amyloidosis

teaching_point: Lichen amyloidosis: very itchy, firm tan-brown scaly papules on the shins, sometimes in rows — potent topical steroid under occlusion is a common specialist approach.
dermnet_caption: Scaly tan brown papules, some arranged lineraly in lichen amyloidosis on the leg
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scaly tan brown papules, some arranged lineraly in lichen amyloidosis on the leg (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-amyloidosis

teaching_point: Extensive confluent lichen amyloidosis on the shin — differentials: hypertrophic lichen planus, lichen simplex chronicus, prurigo; biopsy to confirm.
dermnet_caption: Extensive and confluent lesions of lichen amyloidosis on the shin
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Extensive and confluent lesions of lichen amyloidosis on the shin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-amyloidosis

teaching_point: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation after an inflamed cyst — darker and longer-lasting in skin of colour; treat the underlying inflammation first.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Postinflammatory hyperpigmentation (inflamed cyst) (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/postinflammatory-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: PIH after healed eczema — reassure that pigment fades slowly (months–years for dermal pigment); controlling flares prevents more.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Healed eczema (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/postinflammatory-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: Frictional hyperpigmentation (violin-player's neck) — friction is a key driver of flexural/constitutional pigmentation; remove the friction source.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Violin playing (friction) (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/postinflammatory-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: Pigmentation from lichen planus actinicus — lichenoid inflammation damages the basal layer, causing deep dermal (pigment incontinence) PIH.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lichen planus actinicus (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/postinflammatory-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: PIH after irritant dermatitis — common sequel of harsh cosmetic/home remedies or shaving irritation in the axillae and groin.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Irritant dermatitis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/postinflammatory-hyperpigmentation

teaching_point: Hyperpigmentation due to acne — azelaic acid, topical retinoid and daily sunscreen are UK-licensed, lower-risk first steps before any lightening agent.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hyperpigmentation due to acne (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/hydroquinone

teaching_point: Suntan in dark skin — constitutional skin colour varies and darkens with UV; distinguish normal variation from disease before treating.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Suntan in dark skin (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pigmentation-disorders

teaching_point: Hormonal pigmentation (linea nigra) — physiological in pregnancy; reassure; fades post-partum.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Hormonal pigmentation (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pigmentation-disorders

teaching_point: Piebaldism: congenital, stable, well-demarcated depigmented patches (often ventral trunk/limbs) with white forelock — KIT gene, autosomal dominant; present from birth (vs vitiligo acquired).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Piebaldism (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/piebaldism

teaching_point: Piebaldism on the limbs with islands of normal/hyperpigmented skin within white patches — does not progress or repigment; camouflage, sun protection, genetic counselling.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Piebaldism (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/piebaldism

teaching_point: Piebaldism on the trunk — central/anterior distribution, sparing the back midline; consider Waardenburg syndrome if deafness/heterochromia.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Piebaldism (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/piebaldism

teaching_point: Piebaldism — symmetrical knee/shin patches; family history usually positive; surgical grafting is a specialist option for stable patches.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Piebaldism (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/piebaldism

teaching_point: Non-segmental vitiligo at the wrists — acquired, symmetrical, milky-white under Wood's lamp; can progress; ask about thyroid/autoimmune history.
dermnet_caption: Symmetrical wrist vitiligo - a common location
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Symmetrical wrist vitiligo - a common location (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: Vitiligo over knuckles — Koebner phenomenon (trauma sites); advise avoiding friction/injury.
dermnet_caption: Vitiligo over the knuckles - keobnerisation due to trauma often localises vitiligo
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Vitiligo over the knuckles - keobnerisation due to trauma often localises vitiligo (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: Periocular vitiligo with poliosis (white lashes) — facial/eyelid sites suit topical calcineurin inhibitor (off-label) rather than potent steroid.
dermnet_caption: Vitiligo on the lid with poliosis of the lashes
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Vitiligo on the lid with poliosis of the lashes (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: Extensive symmetrical facial vitiligo in skin of colour — major psychosocial impact; refer for phototherapy/ruxolitinib cream assessment; camouflage service.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Extensive symmetrical facial vitiligo (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: Follicular (perifollicular) repigmentation in vitiligo — sign of treatment response; melanocyte reservoir in hair follicles explains why hairy skin responds better than lips/acral sites.
dermnet_caption: Follicular repigmentation in a patch of vitiligo
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Follicular repigmentation in a patch of vitiligo (© Te Whatu Ora) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/vitiligo

teaching_point: Pityriasis alba on the cheeks — ill-defined, slightly scaly pale patches in atopic children; hypopigmented not depigmented (vs vitiligo); emollient + sun protection.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pityriasis alba on the cheeks (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pigmentation-disorders

teaching_point: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation after longstanding prurigo — more severe injury can leave permanent pale marks; a caution for aggressive peels/lasers in skin of colour.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Longstanding prurigo (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pigmentation-disorders

teaching_point: Clobetasol-containing "spot remover"/bleaching product — illegal skin lighteners may hide potent steroid, hydroquinone or mercury; counsel and report (Trading Standards/MHRA Yellow Card).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermovate cream (Open access image) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/bleaching-agents

teaching_point: Striae from potent topical steroid misuse (e.g. as a lightener) — irreversible atrophy; part of the harm profile alongside steroid acne and infections.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
